title: RCMP shooting inquest delayed again
article: A coroner's inquest into the death of Harry Haineault, the man shot by an RCMP officer almost four years ago, has been abruptly suspended a second time.

In a news release issued Saturday, the province's justice ministry said the inquest, which was to resume Monday after it was first suspended 17 months ago, would be postponed again "as a result of additional information coming to light."
There were no details provided about the nature of the additional information and a communications official with the ministry declined to elaborate.

The inquest had already taken a surprise turn when, just one day into the initial proceedings in 2010, it was learned that video cameras may have recorded some of what happened when Haineault, 38, died.
The inquest was stopped while that matter was examined. It is not known if the latest postponement is related to the videos, which were taken in the yard of the home of Haineault's brother, Walter.
Before the proceedings were interrupted, the coroner's jury heard some of what happened Sept. 2, 2008, from the RCMP who fired the fatal shot.
Const. Jamie Grant testified he confronted Haineault in a wooded area behind Walter Hainault's home.

Grant was waiting in the woods because Haineault was known as a runner, the inquest was told. Grant and another officer were at the home, on the Clearwater River Dene First Nation, in Saskatchewan's north, with a warrant for a man's arrest.
In the woods, the officer and Haineault struggled to the point where Grant pepper-sprayed the man, however the noxious spray had no effect.

"I told him 'Stop resisting. Harry what are you doing?' I didn't know what was going on," Grant told the inquest. Grant said Haineault managed to get him into a headlock and was choking him. He said he felt "the fear of death setting in" and that's when he shot Haineault.
"I panicked. I didn't know what to do," Grant said.
The coroner's inquest was set to resume in Meadow Lake, Sask.

In the release about the postponement, officials said the delay "will provide the opportunity to thoroughly review.... new information. Once the review has been completed, the inquest will be rescheduled."
